Notes: Sub-king of the Danes; killed in battle December 902.
Possibly succeeded Beonna; sub-king named as the father of Æthelberht II.
The last native East Anglian king; acceded at the age of 14 (according to Asser); killed by the Vikings 20 November 869; canonised.
Ruled Mercia from 757 to July 796; jointly ruled with his son Ecgfrith from 787 (who succeeded him and died after ruling for less than five months).

Reign: Acceded c. 630 (ruled jointly with Sigeberht until c. 634).
Notes: Slain in battle, possibly as late as 641; kinsman of Sigeberht.
Nephew of Rædwald and son of Eni; killed, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
Sub-king, known only from numismatic evidence.
Nephew of Anna, Æthelhere and Æthelwold.
Son of Tytila; named imperium by Bede, later interpreted as Bretwalda. The Flores Historiarum gives 599 for Rædwald's accession.
Accession date is from a late mediaeval source; East Anglian independence indicated by ability of Æthelberht to mint his own coins.
Son of Rædwald; murdered by Ricberht.
Possible ruler; "The first to rule over the East Angles", according to Nennius.
Possible ruler; son of Wehha and the king after whom the Wuffingas dynasty is named.
Sub-king, known only from numismatic evidence.
